_about: Sports nerd facts shown on the result card (first one) and in the Nerd facts pop-up (all). Keyed by card id. Each fact: [label, text], kid-friendly, 160 chars max.

nfl-buffalo-bills: Named after Buffalo Bill Cody, the famous Wild West showman, picked in a 1959 fan contest.
Buster Ramsey led the Bills in their first season, 1960.
A founding team of the AFL in 1960. They joined the NFL when the two leagues merged in 1970.
The only team to play in four Super Bowls in a row, after the 1990 to 1993 seasons.
nfl-miami-dolphins: Picked from a 1965 fan contest that drew about 20,000 entries.
George Wilson coached them in their first season, 1966.
The 1972 Dolphins are the only NFL team with a perfect season: 17 wins, 0 losses, and a Super Bowl.
Coach Don Shula has the most wins of any NFL coach ever: 347.
nfl-new-england-patriots: Chosen by fans in 1960 to honor the patriots of the American Revolution, which began in Massachusetts.
Lou Saban coached the Boston Patriots in their first season, 1960.
They were the Boston Patriots until 1971, when they moved to Foxborough and became New England.
Six Super Bowl titles with Tom Brady and coach Bill Belichick, tied for the most ever.
nfl-new-york-jets: They started in 1960 as the New York Titans. They became the Jets in 1963.
Their new stadium sat next to LaGuardia Airport, with jets flying overhead.
Football legend Sammy Baugh coached the Titans in their first season.
Joe Namath promised a win in Super Bowl III in 1969, then delivered it.
nfl-baltimore-ravens: Named after "The Raven," a famous poem by Edgar Allan Poe, who lived in Baltimore. Fans voted for it.
Ted Marchibroda coached them in their first season, 1996.
Formed in 1996 when owner Art Modell moved his team from Cleveland. The Browns name stayed behind.
They won Super Bowls after the 2000 and 2012 seasons.
nfl-cincinnati-bengals: A nod to an earlier Cincinnati Bengals team from the 1930s and 1940s.
Founder Paul Brown also coached them, starting in their first season, 1968.
Their helmets have had orange-and-black tiger stripes since 1981.
nfl-cleveland-browns: Named after their first coach, Paul Brown, after fans picked it in a contest.
Paul Brown, who also invented the face mask and the modern playbook.
Started in 1946 in another league, the AAFC. They won the NFL title in their first NFL season, 1950.
The only NFL team with no logo on its helmet: just plain orange.
nfl-pittsburgh-steelers: Founded by Art Rooney in 1933 as the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Renamed in 1940 to honor the city's famous steel-making industry.
Jap Douds coached them in their first season, 1933.
Their logo sits on only one side of the helmet, and they have six Super Bowl titles.
nfl-houston-texans: Picked in 2000 over other finalists like the Apollos and the Stallions.
Dom Capers coached them in their first season, 2002.
Joined in 2002 as the NFL's 32nd team.
They won their very first game, 19–10 over the Dallas Cowboys.
nfl-indianapolis-colts: Started in Baltimore in 1953 and moved to Indianapolis in 1984.
Named for Maryland's long history of breeding racehorses.
Keith Molesworth coached the Baltimore Colts in their first season, 1953.
Super Bowl champs twice: in Baltimore in 1971 and in Indianapolis in 2007.
nfl-jacksonville-jaguars: Picked by fans in a 1991 contest, years before the team even existed.
Tom Coughlin coached them in their first season, 1995.
They reached the AFC Championship Game in just their second season.
nfl-tennessee-titans: Started in 1960 as the Houston Oilers. They moved to Tennessee in 1997 and became the Titans in 1999.
Nashville is called the "Athens of the South" and has a full-size copy of the Parthenon, so a Greek name fit.
Lou Rymkus coached the Oilers in their first season, 1960.
As the Oilers, they won the first two AFL titles, in 1960 and 1961.
nfl-denver-broncos: Picked in a 1960 fan contest. It was also the name of an earlier Denver baseball team.
Frank Filchock coached them in their first season, 1960.
Fans hated the team's first striped socks so much that they burned them at a 1962 bonfire.
Three Super Bowl titles: after the 1997, 1998 and 2015 seasons.
nfl-kansas-city-chiefs: Started in 1960 as the Dallas Texans and moved to Kansas City in 1963.
Named in honor of Mayor H. Roe Bartle, whose nickname was "The Chief."
Hank Stram coached them from their first season and won Super Bowl IV.
Team founder Lamar Hunt came up with the name "Super Bowl," inspired by his kids' Super Ball toy.
nfl-las-vegas-raiders: Started in Oakland in 1960. They moved to Los Angeles in 1982, back to Oakland in 1995, then to Las Vegas in 2020.
Chosen in a 1960 newspaper contest in Oakland.
Eddie Erdelatz coached them in their first season, 1960.
Three Super Bowl titles, after the 1976, 1980 and 1983 seasons.
nfl-los-angeles-chargers: Started in Los Angeles in 1960. They moved to San Diego in 1961, then came back to LA in 2017.
Owner Barron Hilton liked the "Charge!" cheer that fans yelled at games.
Sid Gillman, a passing-game genius, coached them in their first season.
Their powder-blue jerseys are one of the most loved looks in football.
nfl-dallas-cowboys: Tom Landry coached them for 29 seasons in a row, from their first year in 1960.
Nicknamed "America's Team" after a 1978 highlight film used the phrase.
They've played a home game on Thanksgiving Day almost every year since 1966.
nfl-new-york-giants: Tim Mara bought the team for just $500 in 1925.
They borrowed the name from New York's baseball Giants.
Bob Folwell coached them in their first season, 1925.
In Super Bowl XLII they upset the unbeaten Patriots, thanks to the famous "Helmet Catch."
nfl-philadelphia-eagles: Named in 1933 after the eagle on the badge of the National Recovery Administration, part of the New Deal.
Lud Wray coached them in their first season, 1933.
They won Super Bowl LII with a backup quarterback and a trick play called the "Philly Special."
Super Bowl champs again in February 2025, beating the Chiefs.
nfl-washington-commanders: Started in 1932 as the Boston Braves and moved to Washington in 1937.
Lud Wray coached them in their first season, then moved on to start the Eagles.
In 1937 they became the first NFL team with its own marching band. Three Super Bowl titles.
nfl-chicago-bears: Started in 1920 as the Decatur Staleys, a team paid for by a corn-starch company. They moved to Chicago in 1921.
Football players are bigger than baseball players, so the Cubs' neighbors became the Bears.
George Halas was the team's player, coach and owner. The NFC title trophy is named after him.
The 1985 Bears won the Super Bowl and recorded a hit song, "The Super Bowl Shuffle."
nfl-detroit-lions: Started in 1930 as the Portsmouth Spartans in Ohio and moved to Detroit in 1934.
The lion is the "king of the jungle," a good partner for Detroit's baseball Tigers.
Potsy Clark, their first coach in Detroit, won the 1935 NFL title.
They've played a home game on Thanksgiving almost every year since 1934.
nfl-green-bay-packers: Named after the Indian Packing Company, which paid for their first jerseys in 1919.
Founder Curly Lambeau. Their stadium, Lambeau Field, is named after him.
The only NFL team owned by its fans: hundreds of thousands of people own shares.
They won the first two Super Bowls. The trophy is named after their coach, Vince Lombardi.
nfl-minnesota-vikings: Honors Minnesota's many families with Scandinavian roots.
Norm Van Brocklin coached them in their first season, 1961.
A giant Viking horn, the Gjallarhorn, gets blown before every home game.
Their famous 1970s defense was nicknamed the "Purple People Eaters."
nfl-atlanta-falcons: A schoolteacher, Julia Elliott, won the 1965 naming contest. She said the falcon is "proud and dignified."
Norb Hecker coached them in their first season, 1966.
Their stadium's roof opens and closes like a camera lens.
nfl-carolina-panthers: Joined in 1995 as the team for both North and South Carolina.
Dom Capers coached them in their first season. He later became the Texans' first coach too.
They reached the NFC Championship Game in just their second season, 1996.
nfl-new-orleans-saints: New Orleans got the team on All Saints' Day in 1966, and the jazz song "When the Saints Go Marching In" made it perfect.
Tom Fears coached them in their first season, 1967.
Super Bowl champions after the 2009 season.
nfl-tampa-bay-buccaneers: Named after the pirates of Florida legend. Tampa holds a big pirate festival, Gasparilla, every year.
John McKay coached them in their first season, 1976.
A pirate ship in their stadium blasts cannons every time they score.
With Tom Brady they won Super Bowl LV, the first team to win one in its home stadium.
nfl-arizona-cardinals: The oldest pro football team still running, founded in Chicago in 1898.
Named for their faded maroon jerseys, which someone called "cardinal red."
They moved from Chicago to St. Louis in 1960, then to Arizona in 1988.
nfl-los-angeles-rams: Founded in Cleveland in 1936. They moved to LA in 1946, to St. Louis in 1995, and back to LA in 2016.
Named after the Fordham Rams, a college team.
The first NFL team with a helmet logo. Player Fred Gehrke painted the horns by hand in 1948.
Super Bowl champs after the 1999 season (in St. Louis) and the 2021 season (in LA).
nfl-san-francisco-49ers: Named after the "49ers," the gold seekers who rushed to California in 1849.
Buck Shaw coached them in their first season, 1946.
Joe Montana's pass to Dwight Clark in 1982 is known simply as "The Catch."
nfl-seattle-seahawks: Picked from about 20,000 fan entries in 1975.
Jack Patera coached them in their first season, 1976.
Fans are the "12th Man," and their noise once measured on earthquake sensors.
Super Bowl champions after the 2013 season.
nba-boston-celtics: Named for Boston's many families with Irish (Celtic) roots.
John "Honey" Russell coached them in their first season, 1946.
18 NBA titles, the most ever, including 8 in a row from 1959 to 1966.
nba-brooklyn-nets: Started in 1967 as the New Jersey Americans. They moved to Long Island, back to New Jersey, then to Brooklyn in 2012.
Picked to rhyme with New York's Mets and Jets.
Max Zaslofsky coached them in their first season.
Julius "Dr. J" Erving led them to two ABA titles, in 1974 and 1976.
nba-new-york-knicks: Short for Knickerbockers, an old nickname for New Yorkers, from the rolled-up pants of Dutch settlers.
Neil Cohalan coached them in their first season, 1946.
They played in the league's very first game, in Toronto on November 1, 1946.
nba-philadelphia-76ers: Named for 1776, when the Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia.
Started in 1946 as the Syracuse Nationals and moved to Philadelphia in 1963.
Syracuse owner Danny Biasone invented the 24-second shot clock in 1954.
nba-toronto-raptors: Fans picked it in 1994, the year after the movie Jurassic Park came out.
Brendan Malone coached them in their first season, 1995.
The 2019 NBA champions: the first title won by a team outside the USA.
nba-chicago-bulls: A nod to Chicago's history as a cattle-trading city.
Johnny "Red" Kerr won Coach of the Year in their first season, 1966.
Six titles in the 1990s with Michael Jordan, plus a 72–10 record in 1995–96.
nba-cleveland-cavaliers: Picked in a 1970 newspaper fan contest.
Bill Fitch coached them in their first season, 1970.
In 2016 they came back from 3 games to 1 down to win the title, a first in NBA Finals history.
nba-detroit-pistons: Founder Fred Zollner's factory made pistons for car and truck engines.
Started in 1941 as the Fort Wayne Zollner Pistons in Indiana. They moved to Detroit in 1957.
A 19–18 game they played against the Lakers in 1950 helped lead to the shot clock.
nba-indiana-pacers: Named for Indiana's harness-racing horses, called pacers, and the pace car at the Indy 500.
Larry Staverman coached them in their first season, 1967.
They won three ABA titles before joining the NBA in 1976.
nba-milwaukee-bucks: Fans picked it in 1968 for Wisconsin's white-tailed deer.
Larry Costello coached them in their first season, 1968.
They won the 1971 title in only their third season. Then in 2021, Giannis scored 50 points to win the title again.
nba-atlanta-hawks: They began in 1946 in Buffalo, then played in the Tri-Cities, Milwaukee and St. Louis before reaching Atlanta in 1968.
The legendary coach Red Auerbach coached them in 1949–50, when they were the Tri-Cities Blackhawks.
They won the 1958 NBA title in St. Louis, led by Bob Pettit.
nba-charlotte-hornets: In 1780 a British general called Charlotte "a hornet's nest."
Dick Harter coached them in their first season, 1988.
They played as the Bobcats from 2004 to 2014, then took back the Hornets name and history.
nba-miami-heat: Picked in a 1986 fan contest, a perfect fit for Miami's hot weather.
Ron Rothstein coached them in their first season, 1988.
nba-orlando-magic: A fan contest picked it for the magic of Orlando's theme parks.
Matt Guokas coached them in their first season, 1989.
They won the draft lottery two years in a row, in 1992 and 1993. Their first pick was Shaquille O'Neal.
nba-washington-wizards: They started in 1961 as the Chicago Packers, moved to Baltimore in 1963, then came to the Washington area in 1973.
They became the Wizards in 1997 after a fan contest.
Jim Pollard coached the Chicago Packers in their first season.
nba-denver-nuggets: They started in 1967 as the Denver Rockets and became the Nuggets in 1974.
Named for the gold nuggets found in Colorado's 1858 gold rush.
They won their first title in 2023, led by Nikola Jokić.
nba-minnesota-timberwolves: Minnesota has more gray wolves than any other state in the lower 48. Fans voted for it.
Bill Musselman coached them in their first season, 1989.
More than 1 million fans came in their first season, a record at the time.
nba-oklahoma-city-thunder: Started in 1967 as the Seattle SuperSonics and moved to Oklahoma City in 2008.
Named for the huge thunderstorms that roll across Oklahoma's plains.
Champs as the Sonics in 1979 and as the Thunder in 2025.
nba-portland-trail-blazers: Honors the pioneers who traveled the Oregon Trail.
Rolland Todd coached them in their first season, 1970.
They won the title in 1977, only their seventh season, and then sold out 814 home games in a row.
nba-utah-jazz: They started in 1974 in New Orleans, where jazz was born. When they moved to Utah in 1979, they kept the name.
Scotty Robertson coached them in their first season.
John Stockton holds the NBA career records for assists and steals.
nba-golden-state-warriors: Started in 1946 as the Philadelphia Warriors and moved to the Bay Area in 1962.
Eddie Gottlieb coached them to the league's very first title, in 1947.
Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points in one game for the Philadelphia Warriors in 1962.
nba-la-clippers: They started in 1970 as the Buffalo Braves, moved to San Diego in 1978, then to LA in 1984.
Named for the clipper ships that sailed into San Diego Bay.
Dolph Schayes coached the Buffalo Braves in their first season.
nba-los-angeles-lakers: They started in Minnesota, the "Land of 10,000 Lakes," and kept the name when they moved to LA in 1960.
John Kundla coached them to five titles in Minneapolis.
17 NBA titles, with stars like George Mikan, Magic Johnson, Kobe Bryant and LeBron James.
nba-phoenix-suns: Picked from about 28,000 fan entries in 1968. The winner got $1,000 and season tickets.
Johnny "Red" Kerr coached them in their first season, after starting out with the Bulls.
In 1969 they lost a coin flip for the first draft pick, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.
nba-sacramento-kings: They began as the Rochester Royals, then played in Cincinnati and Kansas City before moving to Sacramento in 1985.
Oscar Robertson averaged a triple-double for the whole 1961–62 season, playing for Cincinnati.
Their arena was the first in the world to run fully on solar power.
nba-dallas-mavericks: Fans voted for it, partly for the TV western Maverick. Its star, James Garner, was an owner.
Dick Motta coached them in their first season, 1980.
Dirk Nowitzki played 21 seasons, all for Dallas, and led them to the 2011 title.
nba-houston-rockets: They started in 1967 in San Diego, a city famous for building rockets, and moved to Houston in 1971.
The name fit Houston too: NASA's Mission Control is there.
Jack McMahon coached them in their first season.
Champions in 1994 and 1995, led by Hakeem Olajuwon.
nba-memphis-grizzlies: Joined the NBA in 1995 in Vancouver, Canada, and moved to Memphis in 2001.
Named for the grizzly bears of British Columbia.
Brian Winters coached them in their first season, 1995.
nba-new-orleans-pelicans: Named for the brown pelican, Louisiana's state bird, which is on the state flag.
The Charlotte Hornets moved to New Orleans in 2002. The team became the Pelicans in 2013.
Paul Silas coached their first New Orleans season.
nba-san-antonio-spurs: Started in 1967 as the Dallas Chaparrals and moved to San Antonio in 1973.
Named for the spurs that cowboys wear on their boots.
Five titles under coach Gregg Popovich, led by Tim Duncan.
mlb-baltimore-orioles: Named for the Baltimore oriole, Maryland's orange-and-black state bird.
Started in 1901 as the Milwaukee Brewers, played as the St. Louis Browns, and moved to Baltimore in 1954.
Jimmie Dykes managed their first Baltimore season.
Cal Ripken Jr. played 2,632 games in a row, a record that still stands.
mlb-boston-red-sox: Started in 1901 as the Boston Americans and became the Red Sox in 1908.
Jimmy Collins managed them in 1903, when they won the first-ever World Series.
Fenway Park, opened in 1912, is the oldest ballpark in the majors. Its left-field wall is called the Green Monster.
mlb-new-york-yankees: Started in 1901 as the Baltimore Orioles, moved to New York in 1903, and became the Yankees in 1913.
Before that they were the Highlanders, because their ballpark sat on high ground.
Clark Griffith managed their first New York season.
27 World Series titles, the most of any team.
mlb-tampa-bay-rays: Started as the Devil Rays, a kind of manta ray. In 2008 they shortened it to Rays, as in rays of sunshine.
Larry Rothschild managed them in their first season, 1998.
In 2008 they went from the worst record in baseball to the World Series in just one year.
mlb-toronto-blue-jays: Fans picked it in 1976 from more than 4,000 names.
Roy Hartsfield managed them in their first season, 1977.
They won the World Series in 1992 and 1993, the first champions from outside the USA.
Their stadium opened in 1989 with the world's first fully retractable, motorized roof.
mlb-chicago-white-sox: Named after the White Stockings, an older Chicago team name.
Clark Griffith played and managed in their first season, 1901.
World Series champs in 2005. Their scoreboard shoots fireworks after home runs.
mlb-cleveland-guardians: Named in 2022 after the "Guardians of Traffic" statues on a bridge near their ballpark.
Jimmy McAleer managed them in their first season, 1901.
Larry Doby joined them in 1947, the first Black player in the American League.
mlb-detroit-tigers: Said to come from the orange-and-black striped socks of their early teams.
George Stallings managed them in their first season, 1901.
Ty Cobb's .366 career batting average is the highest in big-league history.
mlb-kansas-city-royals: Named after the American Royal, a big livestock show held in Kansas City since 1899.
Joe Gordon managed them in their first season, 1969.
Their ballpark has one of the world's largest privately funded fountain displays.
mlb-minnesota-twins: Started in 1901 as the Washington Senators and moved to Minnesota in 1961.
Named for the "Twin Cities," Minneapolis and St. Paul. Their logo shows two players shaking hands across a river.
mlb-athletics: Started in Philadelphia in 1901, then moved to Kansas City in 1955, Oakland in 1968, and Sacramento in 2025. Las Vegas is next.
Connie Mack managed them for 50 seasons in a row, from 1901 to 1950. That's a record.
Their elephant mascot started as a joke by a rival manager, and the team proudly kept it.
mlb-houston-astros: Named in 1965 for the astronauts trained at NASA in Houston.
Harry Craft managed them in their first season, 1962.
In 1965 they opened the Astrodome, the first domed stadium, which led to the invention of AstroTurf.
mlb-los-angeles-angels: Founded in 1961 by Gene Autry, a famous singing cowboy.
Los Angeles means "the angels" in Spanish.
Bill Rigney managed them in their first season, 1961.
A giant "A" sign with a halo stands outside their ballpark. World Series champs in 2002.
mlb-seattle-mariners: Named for Seattle's long history as a busy seaport.
Darrell Johnson managed them in their first season, 1977.
The 2001 Mariners, starring rookie Ichiro Suzuki, won 116 games and tied the all-time record.
mlb-texas-rangers: Started in 1961 as the Washington Senators and moved to Texas in 1972.
Mickey Vernon managed them in their first season, 1961.
Nolan Ryan threw his record seventh no-hitter for them in 1991.
They won their first World Series in 2023.
mlb-atlanta-braves: The oldest pro sports team still playing in America: founded in Boston in 1871.
Harry Wright managed them in their first season, 1871.
They moved to Milwaukee in 1953 and Atlanta in 1966. Hank Aaron hit his 715th home run there in 1974.
mlb-miami-marlins: Named for the marlin, a big, fast game fish, and an old Miami minor-league team.
Rene Lachemann managed them in their first season, 1993.
They won the World Series in 1997, only their fifth season, and again in 2003.
mlb-new-york-mets: Short for Metropolitans, the name of a New York team from the 1880s.
Casey Stengel managed them in their first season, 1962.
Their blue and orange came from the Dodgers and Giants, the two teams that had left New York.
The "Miracle Mets" won the 1969 World Series.
mlb-philadelphia-phillies: Founded in 1883: the oldest team in American sports with the same name in the same city.
Bob Ferguson managed them in their first season, 1883.
World Series champs in 1980 and 2008. Their fuzzy green mascot is the Phillie Phanatic.
mlb-washington-nationals: Started in 1969 as the Montreal Expos, named after the Expo 67 world's fair. They moved to Washington in 2005.
Gene Mauch managed the Expos in their first season.
In the 2019 World Series they won all four of their wins on the road, a first.
mlb-chicago-cubs: Newspapers started calling the team the "Cubs" in 1902 because it had so many young players.
Albert Spalding played and managed in 1876. He also founded the Spalding sports company.
The ivy on Wrigley Field's walls was planted in 1937. Their 2016 title ended a 108-year wait.
mlb-cincinnati-reds: Named after the 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings, baseball's first openly all-pro team.
Cincinnati holds an Opening Day parade every year to honor that history.
The "Big Red Machine" won the World Series in 1975 and 1976.
mlb-milwaukee-brewers: Started in 1969 as the Seattle Pilots and moved to Milwaukee in 1970.
Joe Schultz managed the Pilots in their first season.
In 1998 they became the first modern team to switch leagues, moving from the American League to the National League.
Fans love the sausage race held in the middle of every home game.
mlb-pittsburgh-pirates: In 1891 they signed a player away from another team, and the rival club accused them of acting like pirates.
Bill Mazeroski's home run won the 1960 World Series, the first walk-off homer to end a Series.
They played in the very first modern World Series, in 1903.
mlb-st-louis-cardinals: In 1899 a fan called their red trim "a lovely shade of cardinal," and the name stuck.
11 World Series titles, the most of any National League team.
Stan "The Man" Musial played 22 seasons, all for St. Louis.
mlb-arizona-diamondbacks: Named for the western diamondback, a rattlesnake of the Arizona desert.
Buck Showalter managed them in their first season, 1998.
They won the 2001 World Series in only their fourth season. Their ballpark has a swimming pool past the outfield wall.
mlb-colorado-rockies: Don Baylor managed them in their first season, 1993.
One row of purple seats in their upper deck sits exactly one mile above sea level.
The air is so thin there that they store game balls in a humidor to stop them from flying too far.
mlb-los-angeles-dodgers: In 1890s Brooklyn, people had to dodge the streetcars, so fans were called "trolley dodgers."
Played in Brooklyn starting in 1883 and moved to Los Angeles in 1958.
Jackie Robinson joined the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947 and changed baseball forever.
mlb-san-diego-padres: "Padres" means "fathers" in Spanish. It honors the Spanish friars who founded San Diego in 1769.
Preston Gómez managed them in their first season, 1969.
Tony Gwynn won eight batting titles, all with the Padres.
mlb-san-francisco-giants: In 1885 their manager proudly called his team "my giants!"
Started as the New York Gothams in 1883 and moved to San Francisco in 1958.
Home runs that land in the bay behind right field are called "splash hits."
Willie Mays's over-the-shoulder grab in 1954 is known as "The Catch."
nhl-boston-bruins: Joined in 1924 as the first American team in the NHL.
Owner Charles Adams wanted a name for a big, strong, clever animal. "Bruin" is an old word for bear.
Art Ross was their first coach. The trophy for the league's top scorer is named after him.
Bobby Orr's diving, flying goal won the 1970 Stanley Cup.
nhl-buffalo-sabres: Picked in a fan contest in 1970. A sabre is a curved sword carried by leaders.
Punch Imlach coached them in their first season, 1970.
A spin of a roulette wheel gave them the first pick in 1970, star Gilbert Perreault.
nhl-detroit-red-wings: Started in 1926 as the Detroit Cougars. They became the Falcons, then the Red Wings in 1932.
Their winged-wheel logo fits the "Motor City," home of America's car makers.
Art Duncan coached them in their first season.
Fans toss an octopus on the ice in the playoffs. Its eight arms once stood for the eight wins needed to take the Cup.
nhl-florida-panthers: Named for the Florida panther, the state animal.
Roger Neilson coached them in their first season, 1993.
They won the Stanley Cup two years in a row, in 2024 and 2025.
nhl-montreal-canadiens: Founded in 1909. They are older than the NHL itself.
Their nickname, the "Habs," comes from "Les Habitants," a name for early French settlers.
Jack Laviolette was the team's first captain and coach.
24 Stanley Cups, the most of any team, including five in a row from 1956 to 1960.
nhl-ottawa-senators: Named after the original Ottawa Senators, who won many Stanley Cups in the early 1900s.
Rick Bowness coached them in their first season, 1992.
Ottawa is Canada's capital, where the country's senators work.
nhl-tampa-bay-lightning: Tampa Bay is known as the "lightning capital of North America."
Terry Crisp coached them in their first season, 1992.
In 1992 Manon Rhéaume played goal for them in a preseason game, the first woman to play in an NHL game.
nhl-toronto-maple-leafs: Named in 1927 by Conn Smythe after the maple leaf, the symbol of Canada.
A founding NHL team in 1917, first called the Toronto Arenas.
13 Stanley Cups. Their arena sits right next to Union Station.
nhl-carolina-hurricanes: Started in 1972 as the New England Whalers, became the Hartford Whalers, and moved to North Carolina in 1997.
Named for the Atlantic hurricanes that reach the Carolina coast.
Jack Kelley coached the Whalers in their first season.
nhl-columbus-blue-jackets: Ohio made many of the blue coats worn by Union soldiers in the 1860s.
Dave King coached them in their first season, 2000.
A cannon in their arena booms every time they score.
nhl-new-jersey-devils: Started in 1974 as the Kansas City Scouts and became the Colorado Rockies in 1976. They came to New Jersey in 1982.
Named after the Jersey Devil, a legendary creature said to live in the state's Pine Barrens.
Goalie Martin Brodeur holds the record for career wins: 691. Three Stanley Cups.
nhl-new-york-islanders: They play on Long Island, a huge island east of New York City.
Phil Goyette coached them in their first season, 1972.
They won four Stanley Cups in a row (1980 to 1983) and a record 19 playoff series in a row.
nhl-new-york-rangers: Reporters called them "Tex's Rangers," after Tex Rickard, the boss of Madison Square Garden.
Lester Patrick coached them in their first season, 1926.
In the 1928 Final, 44-year-old coach Patrick played goal himself and won.
Four Stanley Cups, most recently in 1994.
nhl-philadelphia-flyers: Keith Allen coached them in their first season, 1967.
In 1974 they became the first expansion team to win the Stanley Cup, then won it again in 1975.
They once went 35 games in a row without a loss (1979–80), an NHL record.
nhl-pittsburgh-penguins: Named after their first arena, the Civic Arena, which was nicknamed "The Igloo."
Red Sullivan coached them in their first season, 1967.
Five Stanley Cups, led by Mario Lemieux and then Sidney Crosby.
nhl-washington-capitals: Named for Washington, D.C., the U.S. capital.
Jim Anderson coached them in their first season, 1974.
In April 2025 Alex Ovechkin passed Wayne Gretzky to become the NHL's all-time top goal scorer.
nhl-chicago-blackhawks: Named by founder Frederic McLaughlin after his Army unit, which honored the Sauk leader Black Hawk.
Pete Muldoon coached them in their first season, 1926.
One of the NHL's "Original Six." They won the Cup in 2010, 2013 and 2015.
nhl-colorado-avalanche: Started in 1972 as the Quebec Nordiques. They moved to Denver in 1995 and won the Cup in their first season there.
Named for the snow that rumbles down the Rocky Mountains.
Hockey legend Maurice "Rocket" Richard was the Nordiques' very first coach.
nhl-dallas-stars: Started in 1967 as the Minnesota North Stars and moved to Dallas in 1993.
Minnesota's motto is "L'Étoile du Nord," which means "Star of the North."
Wren Blair coached the North Stars in their first season.
nhl-minnesota-wild: Named for Minnesota's wild outdoors. Their logo is an animal's head with a forest and sunset hidden inside.
Jacques Lemaire coached them in their first season, 2000.
Minnesota calls itself the "State of Hockey," with more registered players than any other U.S. state.
nhl-nashville-predators: In 1971, workers in downtown Nashville dug up the fossil of a saber-toothed cat.
Barry Trotz coached them for their first 15 seasons, starting in 1998.
Fans have a famous good-luck tradition: tossing catfish onto the ice.
nhl-st-louis-blues: Named after "Saint Louis Blues," a famous song by W.C. Handy.
Lynn Patrick started the first season. Then Scotty Bowman, the winningest NHL coach ever, took over.
In January 2019 they were last in the NHL. That June they won the Stanley Cup.
nhl-utah-mammoth: Joined in 2024 as the Utah Hockey Club and picked the Mammoth name in 2025.
Fossils of woolly mammoths have been found in Utah.
André Tourigny coached them in their first season.
nhl-winnipeg-jets: Started in 1999 as the Atlanta Thrashers. They moved to Winnipeg in 2011 and brought back the city's old Jets name.
Their logo is a fighter jet, honoring the Royal Canadian Air Force.
At playoff games, fans all wear white for the famous "Winnipeg Whiteout."
nhl-anaheim-ducks: Disney started the team in 1993 and named it after its hit movie The Mighty Ducks.
Ron Wilson coached them in their first season, 1993.
nhl-calgary-flames: Started in 1972 as the Atlanta Flames and moved to Calgary in 1980, keeping the name.
Bernie "Boom Boom" Geoffrion coached Atlanta in their first season. He's said to have helped invent the slapshot.
In 1989 they became the only visiting team to win the Stanley Cup on the Montreal Forum ice.
nhl-edmonton-oilers: Named for Alberta's big oil industry.
Started in 1972 in another league, the WHA, and joined the NHL in 1979.
With Wayne Gretzky they won five Stanley Cups between 1984 and 1990. Today Connor McDavid leads the way.
nhl-los-angeles-kings: Owner Jack Kent Cooke picked a royal name, with royal purple and gold.
Red Kelly coached them in their first season, 1967.
Wayne Gretzky joined in 1988, and hockey took off all over California.
nhl-san-jose-sharks: Named by fans for the many kinds of sharks in the Pacific Ocean near the Bay Area.
George Kingston coached them in their first season, 1991.
Players skate onto the ice through a giant shark head.
nhl-seattle-kraken: The kraken is a giant sea monster from old sailor legends.
Dave Hakstol coached them in their first season, 2021, when they became the NHL's 32nd team.
Their arena kept its famous roof from the 1962 World's Fair.
nhl-vancouver-canucks: "Canuck" is a friendly nickname for Canadians. Johnny Canuck was a comic-book hero.
Hal Laycoe coached them in their first NHL season, 1970.
Twins Daniel and Henrik Sedin played 17 NHL seasons together, all for Vancouver.
nhl-vegas-golden-knights: Owner Bill Foley went to West Point, whose teams are the Black Knights. Gold stands for Nevada's mines.
Gerard Gallant coached them in their first season, 2017.
They reached the Stanley Cup Final in their very first season and won the Cup in 2023.
mls-atlanta-united-fc: Gerardo "Tata" Martino, who later coached Argentina and Lionel Messi's Inter Miami.
They won MLS Cup in 2018, only their second season.
In 2018 a crowd of 72,548 came to watch them, an MLS record at the time.
mls-charlotte-fc: Miguel Ángel Ramírez coached them in their first season.
Their first home game drew 74,479 fans, a record for one MLS game.
mls-chicago-fire: The club was announced in 1997 on the anniversary of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871.
Bob Bradley, who later coached the U.S. men's national team.
In their very first season, 1998, they won both MLS Cup and the U.S. Open Cup.
mls-fc-cincinnati: Started in 2016 in a lower league, the USL, and jumped to MLS in 2019.
They had the best regular-season record in MLS in 2023 and won the Supporters' Shield.
mls-columbus-crew: In 1999 they built the first stadium made just for an MLS team.
mls-d-c-united: Bruce Arena, who later coached the U.S. men's national team.
They won three of the first four MLS Cups: 1996, 1997 and 1999.
mls-inter-miami-cf: Started playing in 2020. David Beckham is one of the owners.
Diego Alonso coached them in their first season.
Lionel Messi joined in 2023 and won the Leagues Cup trophy in his first month.
mls-cf-montreal: Started in 1993 as the Montreal Impact and joined MLS in 2012.
Jesse Marsch coached them in their first MLS season.
Their stadium sits right next to the Olympic Stadium from the 1976 Summer Games.
mls-nashville-sc: Played in the USL from 2018 and joined MLS in 2020.
Gary Smith coached them in their first MLS season.
GEODIS Park holds 30,000 fans, the biggest stadium in the U.S. and Canada built just for soccer.
mls-new-england-revolution: Honors the American Revolution, which began in Massachusetts in 1775.
Frank Stapleton, a former Ireland striker, coached them in their first season, 1996.
In 2021 they set the MLS record for most points in a season: 73.
mls-new-york-city-fc: Joined MLS in 2015, co-owned by Manchester City and the New York Yankees.
Jason Kreis coached them in their first season.
They play at Yankee Stadium while their own stadium is built in Queens. MLS Cup champs in 2021.
mls-new-york-red-bulls: A founding MLS club in 1996, first called the NY/NJ MetroStars.
The energy-drink company Red Bull bought the team in 2006 and renamed it.
French superstar Thierry Henry played for them from 2010 to 2014.
mls-orlando-city-sc: Started in 2010 in a lower league and joined MLS in 2015.
Adrian Heath coached them in both leagues.
Brazilian star Kaká was their first big signing. U.S. Open Cup winners in 2022.
mls-philadelphia-union: Honors the union of the American colonies. Their snake logo comes from a famous Benjamin Franklin cartoon.
Peter Nowak coached them in their first season, 2010.
Their stadium sits on the Delaware River, right under a giant bridge.
mls-toronto-fc: Joined MLS in 2007 as its first Canadian club.
Mo Johnston coached them in their first season.
In 2017 they won a treble: MLS Cup, the Supporters' Shield and the Canadian Championship.
mls-austin-fc: Joined MLS in 2021 as the first major-league pro team in Austin.
Josh Wolff coached them in their first season.
Actor Matthew McConaughey is an owner, and his official title is "Minister of Culture."
mls-colorado-rapids: Bob Houghton coached them in their first season.
mls-fc-dallas: A founding MLS club, called the Dallas Burn until 2005.
Dave Dir coached them in their first season, 1996.
Their stadium is home to the National Soccer Hall of Fame.
mls-houston-dynamo: Picked for Houston's energy industry and its hard-working spirit.
Dominic Kinnear coached them in their first season, 2006.
They won MLS Cup in their first two seasons, 2006 and 2007.
mls-sporting-kansas-city: A founding MLS club in 1996, first called the Kansas City Wiz, then the Wizards.
Ron Newman coached them in their first season.
mls-la-galaxy: Six MLS Cups, the most of any club, most recently in 2024.
David Beckham joined in 2007, and soccer in America got a lot more famous.
mls-los-angeles-fc: Joined MLS in 2018. Owners include Will Ferrell and Magic Johnson.
Bob Bradley, who was also the Chicago Fire's first coach.
In 2022 they won the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup in the same season.
mls-minnesota-united-fc: Their logo is a loon, Minnesota's state bird.
Played in lower leagues from 2010 and joined MLS in 2017.
Adrian Heath coached them in their first MLS season, after starting Orlando City too.
mls-portland-timbers: Named for Oregon's logging history. The name goes back to a Portland team from 1975.
John Spencer coached them in their first MLS season, 2011.
After every home goal, their mascot Timber Joey cuts a slice off a log and gives it to the scorer.
mls-real-salt-lake: "Real" means royal in Spanish, like Real Madrid.
John Ellinger coached them in their first season, 2005.
mls-san-diego-fc: Joined MLS in 2025 as its 30th club.
Mikey Varas coached them in their first season.
A Native American tribe, the Sycuan Band of the Kumeyaay Nation, is one of the owners, a first in MLS.
mls-san-jose-earthquakes: A founding MLS club in 1996, first called the San Jose Clash.
The Bay Area sits on famous fault lines, and the name came from a 1970s San Jose team.
Chris Wondolowski scored 171 goals for them, the most in MLS history.
mls-seattle-sounders: Named after Puget Sound, the big inlet of the Pacific Ocean next to Seattle.
Sigi Schmid coached them in their first MLS season, 2009.
In 2022 they became the first MLS team to win the CONCACAF Champions League.
mls-st-louis-city-sc: Bradley Carnell coached them in their first season.
They finished first in the Western Conference in their first season.
mls-vancouver-whitecaps: Named for the snowy mountain peaks and the white-capped waves around Vancouver.
The name goes back to 1974. They joined MLS in 2011.
The original Whitecaps won the North American Soccer League's Soccer Bowl in 1979.
nwsl-angel-city-fc: Joined the NWSL in 2022. It was founded by actor Natalie Portman.
Its owners include Serena Williams and many former U.S. national team stars.
Freya Coombe coached them in their first season.
nwsl-bay-fc: Joined in 2024, started by four former U.S. national team players, including Brandi Chastain.
Chastain scored the winning penalty in the 1999 Women's World Cup final.
Albertin Montoya coached them in their first season.
nwsl-boston-legacy-fc: The name honors Boston's long history of firsts in American sports.
nwsl-chicago-stars: A founding NWSL club in 2013, first called the Chicago Red Stars.
The stars come from Chicago's city flag, which has four red stars.
Rory Dames coached them for nearly a decade.
nwsl-denver-summit-fc: Named for the high mountain summits of the Colorado Rockies.
nwsl-gotham-fc: A founding NWSL club in 2013, first called Sky Blue FC.
"Gotham" is an old nickname for New York City.
nwsl-houston-dash: Joined the NWSL in 2014 as the sister club of the Houston Dynamo.
Randy Waldrum coached them in their first season.
They won the 2020 NWSL Challenge Cup.
nwsl-kansas-city-current: In 2024 they opened the first stadium in the world built just for a women's pro team.
nwsl-north-carolina-courage: Started in New York as the Western New York Flash and moved to North Carolina in 2017.
Paul Riley coached their first North Carolina seasons.
nwsl-orlando-pride: A group of lions is called a pride, and Orlando City's symbol is a lion.
Tom Sermanni coached them in their first season, 2016.
In 2024, led by Brazilian legend Marta, they won both the NWSL Shield and the championship.
nwsl-portland-thorns: Portland is the "City of Roses," and every rose has thorns.
Cindy Parlow Cone, who later became president of U.S. Soccer.
They won the very first NWSL Championship, in 2013.
nwsl-racing-louisville-fc: A nod to the Kentucky Derby, the most famous horse race in America.
Their purple color is lavender, and their crest has a fleur-de-lis, the symbol of Louisville.
nwsl-san-diego-wave: Casey Stoney coached them in their first season.
They won the NWSL Shield in 2023, only their second season.
nwsl-seattle-reign: Say it out loud: Reign sounds like rain, and Seattle is famous for it.
Laura Harvey coached them in their first season.
nwsl-utah-royals: First played from 2018 to 2020, then came back in 2024.
Laura Harvey coached them in their first season. She had also been the Reign's first coach.
nwsl-washington-spirit: Mike Jorden coached them in their first season.
uslc-birmingham-legion-fc: Started playing in the USL Championship in 2019.
Birmingham is nicknamed the "Magic City" because it grew so fast in the late 1800s.
uslc-brooklyn-fc: Brooklyn FC started a women's team in 2024 and added a men's team in the USL Championship.
Their home field is in Coney Island, next to the famous boardwalk and amusement parks.
uslc-charleston-battery: Named after the Battery, a famous seawall walkway in Charleston.
Founded in 1993, one of the oldest pro soccer clubs still playing in America.
uslc-detroit-city-fc: Started in 2012 as a fan-favorite amateur club and turned pro in 2022.
Their nickname is "Le Rouge," French for "the red," a nod to Detroit's French founders.
Their home, Keyworth Stadium, was built in 1936.
uslc-hartford-athletic: They play at Dillon Stadium, which once hosted big rock concerts.
uslc-indy-eleven: Eleven is the number of players a soccer team has on the field.
uslc-loudoun-united-fc: Started in 2019 as the partner club of D.C. United.
Young players come here to get ready for MLS.
uslc-louisville-city-fc: Their crest has a fleur-de-lis, the symbol of Louisville.
uslc-miami-fc: Founded in 2015 by Italian soccer legend Paolo Maldini and businessman Riccardo Silva.
They play at FIU, Florida International University.
uslc-pittsburgh-riverhounds: Founded in 1999, one of the longest-running clubs in the USL.
Their stadium sits on the riverbank across from downtown, near where Pittsburgh's three rivers meet.
uslc-rhode-island-fc: Khano Smith coached them in their first season.
Their new stadium opened in 2025 on the river in Pawtucket.
uslc-sporting-club-jacksonville: Founded in 2023, with men's and women's teams.
Jacksonville is the biggest city by land area in the lower 48 states.
uslc-tampa-bay-rowdies: The original Rowdies started in 1975 and won the league title in their first season.
Their famous old slogan: "The Rowdies are a kick in the grass!"
They play at Al Lang Stadium, right on the water in downtown St. Petersburg.
uslc-colorado-springs-switchbacks: Switchbacks are the zigzag trails that wind up mountains like Pikes Peak.
Their stadium sits more than 6,000 feet up, one of the highest in pro soccer.
uslc-el-paso-locomotive-fc: Honors El Paso's railroad history: trains helped the city grow.
uslc-las-vegas-lights: Named for the bright neon lights of Las Vegas.
Started playing in 2018 at Cashman Field.
uslc-lexington-sc: Founded in 2021, with men's and women's teams.
Lexington is known as the "Horse Capital of the World."
uslc-monterey-bay-fc: They play on the campus of Cal State Monterey Bay, close to the ocean.
uslc-new-mexico-united: Started playing in 2019 and quickly became one of the USL's best-attended clubs.
They have played at Albuquerque's baseball park, home of the Isotopes. That team's name comes from The Simpsons!
uslc-oakland-roots-sc: The name honors Oakland's deep community roots. Their crest is a tree.
uslc-orange-county-sc: Started in 2011 as the Los Angeles Blues and became Orange County SC in 2017.
uslc-phoenix-rising-fc: In legend, the phoenix is a bird that rises from the ashes. The city of Phoenix is named after it.
Ivory Coast star Didier Drogba played for them and was a part-owner.
uslc-sacramento-republic-fc: They won the league title in their first season, 2014.
Named after the "California Republic" on the state's bear flag. Sacramento is the state capital.
In 2022 they reached the U.S. Open Cup final while playing in a lower league.
uslc-san-antonio-fc: Started playing in 2016, owned by the same group as the San Antonio Spurs.
uslc-fc-tulsa: Started in 2015 as the Tulsa Roughnecks and became FC Tulsa in 2019.
"Roughnecks" was a name for Oklahoma's oil-field workers. It was also the name of a 1978 Tulsa team.
usl1-athletic-club-boise: A brand-new club in USL League One.
Boise is Idaho's capital and its biggest city.
usl1-av-alta-fc: "Alta" means high in Spanish, for the high desert of the Antelope Valley.
A new club in USL League One.
usl1-charlotte-independence: Charlotte celebrates the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, which locals say was signed there in 1775.
usl1-chattanooga-red-wolves: The red wolf is one of the rarest wolves in the world and comes from the American Southeast.
usl1-corpus-christi-fc: A new club in USL League One.
Corpus Christi is a beach city on the Gulf Coast of Texas.
usl1-fort-wayne-fc: Played in an amateur league first, then joined USL League One.
Fort Wayne is Indiana's second-biggest city.
usl1-forward-madison-fc: Their crest has a pink flamingo, a nod to the plastic flamingos found all over Madison.
They play at Breese Stevens Field, built in 1926.
usl1-fc-naples: Naples, Florida is named after Naples, Italy, because both sit on a beautiful bay.
usl1-new-york-cosmos: The original Cosmos signed Pelé in 1975, and the whole country started paying attention to soccer.
German legend Franz Beckenbauer also played for the old Cosmos.
The famous name came back for a new club in USL League One.
usl1-one-knoxville-sc: Started in 2023 and joined USL League One in 2024.
Knoxville sits at the edge of the Great Smoky Mountains.
usl1-richmond-kickers: Founded in 1993, one of the oldest pro soccer clubs in America.
They won the U.S. Open Cup in 1995.
usl1-sarasota-paradise: A new club in USL League One.
Sarasota is famous for its white-sand beaches on the Gulf of Mexico.
usl1-spokane-velocity-fc: Spokane has hosted two world's fairs, in 1974 and 1983.
usl1-westchester-sc: Westchester is the county just north of New York City.
uslsl-brooklyn-fc: A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
They play in Coney Island, home of the famous boardwalk.
uslsl-carolina-ascent-fc: A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
They play in Charlotte, North Carolina's biggest city.
uslsl-dallas-trinity-fc: Named for the Trinity River, which runs through Dallas.
They play at the Cotton Bowl, a stadium that opened in 1930.
uslsl-dc-power-fc: Named for Washington, D.C., home of the most powerful offices in the country.
A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
uslsl-fort-lauderdale-united-fc: A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
Fort Lauderdale has so many canals that people call it the "Venice of America."
uslsl-lexington-sc: A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
Lexington is known as the "Horse Capital of the World."
uslsl-sporting-club-jacksonville: Joined the USL Super League in 2025.
Jacksonville is the biggest city by land area in the lower 48 states.
uslsl-tampa-bay-sun-fc: A founding club of the USL Super League in 2024.
They won the very first USL Super League final, in 2025.
liverpool: Founded in 1892, when Everton moved out of Anfield and the stadium's owner started a new club to play there.
Fans sing "You'll Never Walk Alone" before every home game.
Six European Cups, the most of any English club.
newcastle: Formed in 1892 when two local clubs, Newcastle East End and West End, joined together.
Nicknamed the Magpies for their black-and-white striped shirts.
They won the 2025 League Cup, their first major home trophy in 70 years.
arsenal: Started in 1886 by workers at the Royal Arsenal factory in Woolwich, south London. They moved north in 1913.
Manager Herbert Chapman got the local Underground station renamed "Arsenal" in 1932.
In 2003–04 they went the whole league season unbeaten.
realmadrid: "Real" means royal: King Alfonso XIII gave the club the title in 1920.
15 European Cups, far more than any other club.
The Santiago Bernabéu stadium is named after the club's longtime president.
barcelona: Founded in 1899 by Joan Gamper, a Swiss player who placed a newspaper ad looking for teammates.
Their motto is "Més que un club," Catalan for "More than a club."
Lionel Messi scored 672 goals for Barça, the club record.
athletic: English spelling because English miners and students helped start the club in 1898.
With Real Madrid and Barcelona, they're one of only three clubs that have played in every La Liga season.
Their stadium, San Mamés, is nicknamed "La Catedral," the Cathedral.
toulouse: More French championship titles than any other club. The trophy is a shield, the Bouclier de Brennus.
Superstar Antoine Dupont, often called the best player in the world, plays here.
racing92: Started in 1882 as Racing Club de France, one of the oldest sports clubs in France.
The 92 is the number of the Paris-area department where they play, Hauts-de-Seine.
In the 1990 final, their players wore pink bow ties on the field, and they won.
clermont: Founded in 1911 by workers at the Michelin tyre company, which still backs the club.
Their stadium is named Stade Marcel-Michelin.
Their yellow-and-blue fans are some of the loudest in France.
wimbledon: The All England Club began in 1868 as a croquet club. Tennis came in 1877.
Players must wear almost all white.
Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic have each won the men's title many times. Martina Navratilova won the women's title a record 9 times.
roland-garros: Named after Roland Garros, a French pilot. In 1913 he became the first person to fly across the Mediterranean Sea.
Rafael Nadal won here 14 times, more than any player at any Grand Slam.
The red clay is crushed brick spread on top of limestone.
italian-open: It's played at the Foro Italico in Rome, a sports park lined with 60 giant marble statues of athletes.
One of the biggest clay tournaments before the French Open.
madrid-open: The Caja Mágica, or "Magic Box," has three courts with roofs that slide open and shut.
Madrid is high up, so the ball flies faster here than at most clay events.
monte-carlo: Played at the Monte-Carlo Country Club, with the Mediterranean Sea right behind the courts.
Rafael Nadal won here 8 years in a row, from 2005 to 2012.
atp-finals: Only the year's eight best men's singles players get in.
It moved to Turin, Italy in 2021, after many years in London.
paris-masters: It moved in 2025 to Paris La Défense Arena, a giant indoor stadium.
It's played indoors in late autumn, at the end of the season.
queens-club: Queen's Club opened in 1886 and is named after Queen Victoria.
Players use it to warm up on grass right before Wimbledon.
halle: The stadium's roof can close in about 90 seconds.
Roger Federer won here 10 times, and a street outside is named after him.
hamburg: It's played at the Rothenbaum tennis center, near Hamburg's Alster lake.
basel: Roger Federer was a ball kid here, then won the title 10 times in his hometown.
Played indoors at the St. Jakobshalle every October.
barcelona-open: The center court is called Pista Rafa Nadal, after their 12-time champion.
The Real Club de Tenis Barcelona was founded in 1899.
gstaad: Played about 3,450 feet up in the Swiss Alps.
One of the highest pro tennis tournaments in Europe, and the thin air makes the ball fly.
kitzbuhel: Kitzbühel is a famous Austrian ski town with one of the world's hardest downhill ski races.
Thin mountain air makes the clay courts play fast.
stuttgart: The winner traditionally gets a Porsche sports car.
It's played on clay, but indoors.
vienna-open: Played indoors at the Wiener Stadthalle every October.
One of the biggest indoor tournaments of the season.
rugby-england: Twickenham was built on an old cabbage garden, so it's nicknamed "the Cabbage Patch."
The tournament began in 1883 between England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland.
England won the 2003 Rugby World Cup.
rugby-france: Stade de France opened in 1998, built for the football World Cup.
France joined the tournament in 1910, making it the Five Nations.
France's rugby team is nicknamed "Les Bleus," for their blue shirts.
rugby-wales: The Principality Stadium was built for the 1999 Rugby World Cup.
Welsh fans are famous for singing hymns in the stands.
Wales has won the Grand Slam (beating every team in one Six Nations) many times.
rugby-scotland: Murrayfield opened in 1925 and is Scotland's largest stadium.
Scotland and England play for the Calcutta Cup, the oldest trophy in international rugby, from 1879.
rugby-ireland: One Ireland rugby team represents both Ireland and Northern Ireland.
Ireland has been ranked number one in the world.
rugby-italy: Italy joined in 2000, turning the Five Nations into the Six Nations.
The Stadio Olimpico was built for the 1960 Rome Olympics.
eagles: Joined in 1987 as the league's first club from Western Australia.
Ron Alexander coached them in their first season.
In 1992 they became the first club from outside Victoria to win the premiership.
crows: Joined in 1991 as South Australia's first club in the league.
Graham Cornes coached them in their first season.
Premiers in 1997 and 1998, back to back.
swans: Started as South Melbourne in 1874. They moved to Sydney in 1982.
Their 2005 premiership was the club's first in 72 years.
Their red and white colors go all the way back to South Melbourne.
broncos: Wayne Bennett coached them for their first 21 seasons and won six premierships.
Rugby league is the biggest winter sport in Queensland.
storm: Joined the league in 1998 as the only club in Victoria.
Chris Anderson coached them in their first season.
They won the premiership in 1999, only their second season.
nzwarriors: Joined the league in 1995 as the Auckland Warriors.
John Monie coached them in their first season.
The only NRL club from New Zealand, across the Tasman Sea.
scorchers: Named for Perth's scorching hot summers.
The most successful team in Big Bash history, with five titles.
sixers: Named after the six, cricket's biggest hit: over the boundary without a bounce.
hurricanes: A fitting name for the island of Tasmania, which gets blasted by strong Southern Ocean winds.
They won their first Big Bash title in January 2025.
